events.title: Gregorian Calendar Takes Effect Following Skipped Dates
events.description: In Catholic countries such as Italy, Spain, Portugal, and Poland-Lithuania, October 15, 1582 was the first day of the Gregorian calendar, following Thursday, October 4 of the Julian calendar. Ten days were skipped to correct drift in the calendar's alignment with the solar year, as decreed by Pope Gregory XIII.
events.significance: The Gregorian calendar became the most widely used civil calendar in the world, standardizing timekeeping and the calculation of dates, including Easter.

events.title: Napoleon Arrives on Saint Helena
events.description: Following his defeat at Waterloo, Napoleon Bonaparte arrived on the remote South Atlantic island of Saint Helena aboard HMS Northumberland to begin his final exile under British guard.
events.significance: His exile ended the Napoleonic era in Europe; he remained on the island until his death in 1821, and the Congress of Vienna order was secured.

events.title: Birth of Friedrich Nietzsche
events.description: Friedrich Nietzsche, the German philosopher, cultural critic, and philologist, was born in Röcken, in the Prussian Province of Saxony.
events.significance: Nietzsche's works, including Thus Spoke Zarathustra and Beyond Good and Evil, profoundly influenced existentialism, postmodernism, and modern Western thought.

events.title: Execution of Mata Hari
events.description: Margaretha Zelle, the Dutch exotic dancer known as Mata Hari, was executed by a French firing squad at Vincennes after being convicted of espionage for Germany during World War I.
events.significance: Her case became one of history's most famous spy stories, though historians have since questioned the strength of the evidence against her.

events.title: Vietnam Moratorium Protests
events.description: Millions of Americans took part in demonstrations, rallies, and vigils across the United States as part of the Moratorium to End the War in Vietnam, one of the largest anti-war protests in American history.
events.significance: The Moratorium demonstrated the breadth of public opposition to the Vietnam War and put pressure on the Nixon administration's war policy.
